messages.subject: ggvis 0.4 can't pass string list to filter anymore
messages.subject_clean: ggvis 0.4 can't pass string list to filter anymore
messages.body_plain:
I recently updated ggvis and I am now getting an error when I use filter in one of my plots. The error is:

    "Error in filter(., area %in% eval(input_checkboxgroup(unique(rel_data$area),  : (list) object cannot be coerced to type 'double'"

Here's a reproducible example:

    names = c("Bacilli", "Actinobacteria", "area")
    b_counts <- c(1,5,8,100,34)
    a_counts <- c(1,3,11,55,67)
    area <- c("Gut", "Skin", "Gut", "Gut", "Skin")
    rel_data <- data.frame(b_counts, a_counts, area)
    names(rel_data) <- names

    library(ggvis)

    rel_data %>% ggvis(x = input_select(names(rel_data[,-3]), map = as.name <http://as.name>, label = "X Axis"),
                   y = input_select(names(rel_data[,-3]), map = as.name <http://as.name>, label = "Y Axis")) %>%
      filter(area %in% eval(input_checkboxgroup(unique(rel_data$area), selected = "Gut")))

*Changed old post so I could include a reproducible example

messages.subject: Using group_by, in the presence of a "key" variable, via shiny
messages.subject_clean: Using group_by, in the presence of a "key" variable, via shiny
messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to draw multiple paths efficiently by grouping the data using group_by.  I also want a "key" variable for future handling of mouse events.  Using ggvis (0.4.1) + shiny (0.11.1) + dplyr (0.4.1).

I can't work out why this draws only one of the paths corresponding to the three groups in the data:

mtc <- mutate(mtcars, id=factor(1:nrow(mtcars)))
runApp(list(
    ui = bootstrapPage(
        ggvisOutput("ggvis")
    ),
    server = function(input, output) {
        mtc %>% group_by(cyl) %>% ggvis(~wt, ~mpg, key:=~id, stroke = ~factor(cyl)) %>% layer_paths() %>%
          bind_shiny("ggvis")
    }
))

whereas running ggvis directly, bypassing shiny, gets all three paths drawn.

mtc %>% group_by(cyl) %>% ggvis(~wt, ~mpg, key:=~id, stroke = ~factor(cyl)) %>% layer_paths()

It also works via shiny if the key is removed from the ggvis() call.

In the non-working shiny version, it sometimes draws all three paths, and then immediately redraws using only one of them.

Chris

messages.subject: Re: Horizontal or vertical lines in ggvis
messages.subject_clean: Horizontal or vertical lines in ggvis
messages.body_plain:
Andrew,
I was just searching how to do the same thing. However, the error you are hitting now is because layer_lines() does not take an optional data set the way layer_points() does, such that you cannot override the traditional inheritance. However, you'll notice that earlier in the thread, there was a suggestion to use layer_paths() which does take the optional data set.
-Daniel

messages.subject: Re: Treatment of NA in time series with layer_lines()
messages.subject_clean: Treatment of NA in time series with layer_lines()
messages.body_plain:
Did anyone find a solution to this? I have found the same problem, but the na values are in the middle of the data, so the filling with the maximum values are even more obvious, and more difficult to fix (could do na.interp I guess, but that could be missleading).

I have found that if the renderer is set to canvas rather than SVG the plot will interpolate rather than just showing the maximum. Either by clicking in the browser, or adding this to the ggvis() command:
%>% set_options(renderer="canvas")

Ideally, the plot would show a gap when there is no data.

On Sunday, February 8, 2015 at 7:03:29 PM UTC+10:30, Peter Ellis wrote:
> In my line of work I often have  a time series that begins with a bunch of NAs before real values come in.  I often want the plot to cover the whole period including the NAs, but ggvis seems to default to plotting the NA values at the maximum value or (oddly) just slightly higher than the maximum value.  This is rarely the desired behaviour eg see below.  I could probably contrive a workaround (remove the NA data altogether, and then force the x axis still to start at the beginning of the original data), but is there a simpler way of dealing with this?
>
>
> library(ggvis)
>
> na_eg <- data.frame(
>    period = 1:20,
>    value = c(rep(NA, 10), rnorm(10) + 1:10)
>    )
>
> na_eg %>%
>    ggvis(x = ~period, y = ~value) %>%
>    layer_lines()
>
>  <https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/-vctMRmJn_GQ/VNce4cCAf6I/AAAAAAAAAJ8/a8dC9anKoYo/s1600/NA%2Beg.png>
>

Thanks Hadley.  Great to hear more work is planned for ggvis, though I'm pretty impressed with it already, particularly the animation features.  It's been able to do everything I've asked of it so far.

Any other suggestion to draw multiple disconnected lines efficiently and with clean code?  Otherwise I'll use a for-loop to build up the layers.  In my app they're just straight lines, so an equivalent of geom_segment would also be useful for this - hope this is in the works.

Chris

On Monday, March 30, 2015 at 4:48:22 PM UTC+1, Hadley Wickham wrote:
> It's probably a bug in how we send the data :/
>
> I'm planning to spend ~6 months on ggvis later in the year, so there
> will hopefully be some progress on this and other problems.
>
> Hadley
>
> On Tue, Mar 24, 2015 at 10:19 AM, Chris Jackson
> <chris....@mrc-bsu.cam.ac.uk> wrote:
> > I'm trying to draw multiple paths efficiently by grouping the data using
> > group_by.  I also want a "key" variable for future handling of mouse events.
> > Using ggvis (0.4.1) + shiny (0.11.1) + dplyr (0.4.1).
> >
> > I can't work out why this draws only one of the paths corresponding to the
> > three groups in the data:
> >
> > mtc <- mutate(mtcars, id=factor(1:nrow(mtcars)))
> > runApp(list(
> >     ui = bootstrapPage(
> >         ggvisOutput("ggvis")
> >     ),
> >     server = function(input, output) {
> >         mtc %>% group_by(cyl) %>% ggvis(~wt, ~mpg, key:=~id, stroke =
> > ~factor(cyl)) %>% layer_paths() %>%
> >           bind_shiny("ggvis")
> >     }
> > ))
> >
> > whereas running ggvis directly, bypassing shiny, gets all three paths drawn.
> >
> > mtc %>% group_by(cyl) %>% ggvis(~wt, ~mpg, key:=~id, stroke = ~factor(cyl))
> > %>% layer_paths()
> >
> > It also works via shiny if the key is removed from the ggvis() call.
> >
> > In the non-working shiny version, it sometimes draws all three paths, and
> > then immediately redraws using only one of them.
> >
> > Chris

messages.subject: Re: Treatment of NA in time series with layer_lines()
messages.subject_clean: Treatment of NA in time series with layer_lines()
messages.body_plain:
You could do this trick to get around the problem of the "y-axis" values having NA's (make both the x and y values NA, not just one of them):

library(ggvis)

na_eg <- data.frame(
    period = 1:20,

    value = c(2, 1, rep(NA, 8), rnorm(10) + 1:10)
)

na_eg[is.na <http://is.na>(na_eg$value), "period"] <- NA

na_eg2 <- na_eg[!is.na <http://is.na>(na_eg$value),]

na_eg2 %>%

    ggvis(x = ~period, y = ~value) %>%

    layer_lines() %>% layer_points()

Note in the above example that I added layer_points just to show that the line moves from the second point to the 10th point without plotting any points in between.

An aside, but when I do this (for the above example)

na_eg %>%
    ggvis(x = ~period, y = ~value) %>%

    layer_lines() %>% layer_points()

I get the line draw back to the y-axis strangely (see screenshot attached).  Looks like a bug.

On Saturday, March 28, 2015 at 4:58:43 PM UTC-4, Matt Gibbs wrote:
> Did anyone find a solution to this? I have found the same problem, but the na values are in the middle of the data, so the filling with the maximum values are even more obvious, and more difficult to fix (could do na.interp I guess, but that could be missleading).
>
> I have found that if the renderer is set to canvas rather than SVG the plot will interpolate rather than just showing the maximum. Either by clicking in the browser, or adding this to the ggvis() command:
> %>% set_options(renderer="canvas")
>
> Ideally, the plot would show a gap when there is no data.
>
> On Sunday, February 8, 2015 at 7:03:29 PM UTC+10:30, Peter Ellis wrote:
> > In my line of work I often have  a time series that begins with a bunch of NAs before real values come in.  I often want the plot to cover the whole period including the NAs, but ggvis seems to default to plotting the NA values at the maximum value or (oddly) just slightly higher than the maximum value.  This is rarely the desired behaviour eg see below.  I could probably contrive a workaround (remove the NA data altogether, and then force the x axis still to start at the beginning of the original data), but is there a simpler way of dealing with this?
> >
> >
> > library(ggvis)
> >
> > na_eg <- data.frame(
> >    period = 1:20,
> >    value = c(rep(NA, 10), rnorm(10) + 1:10)
> >    )
> >
> > na_eg %>%
> >    ggvis(x = ~period, y = ~value) %>%
> >    layer_lines()
